title: Averaging and tracking of local attractors in slowly varying systems with two time scales
summary: The paper analyzes to what extent the dynamics of a nonautonomous $n$-dimensional dynamical system with two time scales, formulated in the slow time as $dx/dt=f(t/\varepsilon, t, x)$, can be approximated for small values of $\varepsilon$ by the dynamics of the averaged system $dz/dt=\hat f(t,z)$. Assuming that the skewproduct flow associated with the averaged system admits a local attractor $\mathcal{A}$, we prove that the solutions of the original system whose initial data lie in the basin of attraction of $\mathcal{A}$ track the fibers of the inflated attractor for all positive times.
